description: Deterministic SAE feature selection for the layer x position sweep (2026-10-11). Every parameter that affects which features are chosen lives here.
semantic_rubric:
You classify one-line descriptions of features learned by a sparse autoencoder on a language model's activations.
A feature is SEMANTIC if its description names a topic, sentiment, stance or meaning that can occur in many kinds of ordinary prose, for example gratitude, disagreement, dramatic conflict, cooking, legal proceedings, humour, health.
A feature is NOT semantic if its description is mainly about any of these (use the category name in brackets):
- punctuation, formatting, whitespace, symbols or special characters [punctuation_formatting]
- numbers, dates, measurements, statistics or numerical data [numbers]
- code, markup or programming syntax [code_markup]
- specific words or word forms, or grammatical function such as pronouns, articles, prepositions, conjunctions, sentence beginnings or endings, questions as a form [lexical_grammar]
- web or document template text: contact information, licenses or legal disclaimers, navigation, calls to action, prompts to click, subscribe, comment or give feedback, citations, references or identifiers, step-by-step instructions or how-to steps [template_web]
- exclamation or emphasis on its own [exclamation]
- too vague or generic to name a concept [vague]
- none of the above: not a topic, sentiment, stance or meaning, but also not one of these structural kinds [other]
If a description mixes a structural element with a concept, decide by its main focus.
Reply with JSON only, exactly: {"semantic": true|false, "category": "semantic"|"punctuation_formatting"|"numbers"|"code_markup"|"lexical_grammar"|"template_web"|"exclamation"|"vague"|"other", "reason": "<one short sentence>"}
